title: 11 overlapping status labels with no glossary — `EvidenceTable.jsx` renders draft/submitted/pending/pending_review/pending_confirmation/under_review/approved/active/closed/rejected/archived; `approved` and `active` look identical
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceTable.jsx:138-151` — status badge renderer; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.model.js:60-65` (actual status enum)
**Root Cause:** Confirmed unchanged AND now shown to be worse: `EvidenceTable.jsx:141-151` still renders all 11 original overlapping labels (draft/submitted/pending/pending_review/pending_confirmation/under_review/approved/active/closed/rejected/archived) with the same color collisions (approved, active, AND closed all render green). But the backend `Evidence.model.js` schema enum has since been narrowed to just 8 clean, non-overlapping states: `draft, submitted, assigned, under_review, needs_revision, closed, expired, archived` — `pending`, `pending_review`, `pending_confirmation`, `approved`, `active`, and `rejected` can no longer actually occur as a stored status. The frontend now has dead branches for statuses the backend can never produce, while having NO explicit handling for real current states (`assigned`, `needs_revision`, `expired`) — a frontend/backend status-model drift on top of the original ambiguity problem.
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN, and the underlying status model has drifted from what the UI renders — this needs a UI rewrite against the real 8-state enum, not just cosmetic tooltip additions.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceTable.jsx

1. Replace the STATUS_CONFIG map entirely to match the real backend enum: draft, submitted, assigned, under_review, needs_revision, closed, expired, archived — remove dead entries for pending/pending_review/pending_confirmation/approved/active/rejected.
2. Assign each of the 8 real states a visually distinct color (no two active states sharing the same color).
3. Wrap each badge in a Tooltip with a one-line description of what the state means and what action (if any) is next.
4. Add a regression test asserting every value in evidence.model.js's status enum has a corresponding STATUS_CONFIG entry, to catch future drift automatically.
```

title: Same user can map evidence and approve the same mapping — no self-review prevention in `ControlMappingContent.jsx`; user with `evidence.write` + `evidence.approve` can create and immediately approve; violates A.5.3

This is enforced server-side, so it cannot be bypassed even though the frontend (`ControlMappingContent.jsx`'s `handleApproveMapping`, lines 285-327) still has no equivalent client-side check/disabled-button — a minor residual UX gap (user sees the Approve button enabled then gets a 403) but the actual security/compliance control is in place.

The remaining gap is purely a frontend rendering gap, not a backend data-availability gap — a smaller fix than originally scoped.

**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/EvidenceVersionsContent.jsx`, `integration-hub/VersionTimeline.jsx`

**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
Backend — evidence version endpoint:
1. Include sha256Hash in version response: fetch from S3 via s3.headObject({ Bucket, Key }).Metadata.sha256.

Frontend — EvidenceVersionsContent.jsx:
2. Add "SHA-256" column to the version table.
3. Render as monospace truncated string with copy-to-clipboard button.
4. Tooltip: "SHA-256 computed at upload. Compare with your local file hash to verify integrity."

Frontend — VersionTimeline.jsx:
5. Show hash alongside version timestamp.
```

title: Version diff compares metadata only — file content changes invisible; `FileComparisonTable.jsx` compares fields not file bytes; swapped file attachment shows no change in diff view; violates Clause 7.5.3
description:

**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/FileComparisonTable.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `FileComparisonTable.jsx` shows field-level diff for metadata (title, description, tags, status) but never compares the actual files between versions. A file-swap attack (replacing an approved PDF with different content while keeping identical metadata) would appear as "no changes" in the diff.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: FileComparisonTable.jsx

1. Add a "Files" section to the diff output.
2. For each file in versionA.files and versionB.files, compare: filename, fileSize, mimeType, sha256Hash.
3. If sha256Hash differs: render prominent warning <Alert variant="destructive">File content changed — this is a different file.</Alert>
4. Backend version comparison endpoint: include file-level metadata (name, size, mime, sha256) in both version snapshots.
```

title: Average review time uses `createdAt→updatedAt` gap, not actual review duration — `updatedAt` changes on every edit, inflating reported review time; violates Clause 9.1
description:
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN — `AnalyticsContent.jsx:115-122` confirmed unchanged: `avgDays = reviewedItems.reduce((sum, e) => sum + (new Date(e.updatedAt) - new Date(e.createdAt)) / 86400000, 0) / reviewedItems.length`, with the code's own comment '// Average review time: days between createdAt and updatedAt for approved items' still present.

**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/AnalyticsContent.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `updatedAt` changes on every edit to an evidence record. Calculating review time as `updatedAt - createdAt` inflates the metric significantly for evidence items edited multiple times before review, making the reported average meaningless.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
Backend — evidence schema:
1. Add: submittedAt: Date (set when status → 'submitted')
2. Add: reviewedAt: Date (set when status → 'approved' or 'rejected')

Backend — analytics endpoint:
3. Compute: AVG(reviewedAt - submittedAt) for items where both timestamps exist.

Frontend — AnalyticsContent.jsx:
4. Use server-computed metric from GET /evidence/analytics/summary.
5. Backfill submittedAt/reviewedAt from WorkflowEntry records for existing evidence items (one-time migration).
```

title: Framework coverage formula inflated by non-applicable controls — denominator = total mapping count including non-applicable; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; Annex A SoA requirements
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; ISO 27001 Annex A SoA requirements
description:
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN — grepped `AnalyticsContent.jsx` for `not_applicable`/`notApplicable`/`applicable`, zero matches; no SoA-applicability exclusion logic found in the coverage calculation.

**Files:** Backend coverage calculation service; `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/CoverageScoreCard.jsx`
**Root Cause:** The coverage percentage divides mapped controls by all framework controls including those marked "Not Applicable" in the Statement of Applicability (SoA). Non-applicable controls should be excluded from the denominator, but their inclusion deflates the coverage score and misrepresents compliance posture. This violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3 SoA requirements.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
Backend — coverage calculation service:
1. Accept organizationId param.
2. Query the SoA service (or a local notApplicable field on control-mappings model) for excluded controls.
3. Filter denominator: applicableControls = allControls.filter(c => !soaExclusions.includes(c.id))
4. Return { covered, applicable, notApplicable, formula: string } from the coverage endpoint.

Frontend — CoverageScoreCard.jsx:
5. Show: "67% (47/70 applicable controls)"
6. Add line: "12 controls marked Not Applicable per SoA"
```
